statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and five representative paths.

page.framework: Server-rendered multi-page site with jQuery and third-party advertising/analytics
page.notes: Japanese public news portal. Audited home, category, ranking, article, and recovery state. Search submission, video playback, account/external Docomo journeys, every category, and live-network failure injection were not covered because they are separate or mutable journeys; representative shared templates were de-duplicated.

paths.description: Homepage and primary news-listing template; tested desktop, 360px mobile, dark, contrast, reduced motion, performance, privacy, accessibility, no-JS, and memory.
Society category listing, representing topical section/list templates.
Popularity ranking template, representing ranked/list navigation.
Direct news article, representing reading, publisher metadata, canonical/share metadata, and no-JS content.
Nonexistent route, representing error explanation and recovery.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance and file size to the light capture; white surfaces and dark text remain unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare `color-scheme: light dark` and express surfaces, text, borders, icons, and controls with preference-aware tokens or `light-dark()`.

findings.summary: Low-contrast metadata does not adapt for contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured date/time text at 2.95:1 (#969696 on white), while the prefers-contrast: more capture retained the same palette.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise metadata contrast to at least 4.5:1 and add a prefers-contrast/forced-colors treatment that preserves control and text visibility.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS probe found no `view-transition` CSS on this multi-page news site; representative category, ranking, and article navigations perform full abrupt swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }`, stable `view-transition-name` values, and reduced-motion-safe transitions for navigation context.

findings.summary: The long news pages provide no scroll-state-aware navigation or progress cue.
findings.evidence: Screenshots show long multi-section pages, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state container-query or progress treatment; page chrome does not communicate reading position.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sticky chrome plus scroll-state queries or a lightweight reading-progress affordance on long article/listing pages.

findings.summary: Mobile viewports receive a scaled-down 768px tablet layout.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360×800 viewport, layout metrics reported `innerWidth: 769`, visual scale 0.46875, and the screenshot shows desktop columns and tiny text compressed into the screen. The viewport meta is only `width=device-width`.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a true narrow layout: add `initial-scale=1`, remove the 768px minimum canvas, and use intrinsic grid/flex sizing with fluid type and spacing.

findings.summary: Repeated news components do not respond to their available container.
findings.evidence: The probe found no `@container`; the same cards stay in tablet-scale columns on 360px instead of reflowing for the narrow container.
findings.suggestedFix: Set containment on reusable regions and use container queries/intrinsic sizing so cards, nav, and sidebars recompose where embedded.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is suppressed and some touch targets are undersized.
findings.evidence: The focus probe repeatedly returned outline style `none`; Lighthouse also found 16px-tall publisher links with less than the 24px WCAG 2.2 target-size floor. The scaled tablet viewport further shrinks effective controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a high-contrast `:focus-visible` indicator and provide at least 24×24 CSS px targets with adequate spacing, preferably 44px for primary mobile controls.

findings.summary: Cold mobile loading is far outside the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 7.4s, LCP 11.6s, Speed Index 13.5s, TBT 360ms, and a performance score of 47. The separate trace still measured LCP 3.35s, above the 2.5s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, shorten the critical chain, defer nonessential scripts, and validate under mobile throttling until LCP is ≤2.5s and interaction blocking is low.

findings.summary: Third-party and legacy JavaScript consume substantial main-thread time.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 5.3s main-thread work, 3.1s JavaScript execution, TTI 28s, and TBT 360ms; the trace recorded a 79ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary execution, split first-party work, delay analytics/ads until after content and consent, and chunk remaining tasks below 50ms.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking scripts and weak delivery delay content.
findings.evidence: HAR plus DOM confirmation found six classic scripts in `<head>` with neither async nor defer, including 282KB `swiper.js`; Lighthouse estimated 4.64s render-blocking savings and flagged cache, font-display, HTTP, and dependency-tree issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or module-load noncritical scripts, inline only minimal critical CSS, compress text, set durable immutable caching for versioned assets, and use `font-display` with stable fallbacks.

findings.summary: The page ships large amounts of unused and legacy code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,392KiB unused JavaScript, 157KiB unused CSS, 130KiB legacy JavaScript, and 82KiB unminified JavaScript; HAR attributes 1.30MB to scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete or conditionally load unused features, tree-shake and modernise bundles, deduplicate tags, and defer below-fold rendering.

findings.summary: A search field lacks an accessible label.
findings.evidence: axe reported a critical `label` violation for `input#search`; Lighthouse independently found unlabeled search input `#queryft`.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate visible `<label>` elements or precise accessible names with every search input and verify the accessibility tree on all templates.

findings.summary: News timestamps fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured repeated 12px timestamp text at 2.95:1 against white, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken secondary text or adjust its background so normal-size text reaches at least 4.5:1 in every state.

findings.summary: Heading/landmark structure and focus presentation are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: axe found skipped heading levels and non-unique landmarks; the probe ends an H1/H2/H3 sequence with H4 and found no visible computed outline on focused controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sequential headings based on document hierarchy, uniquely label repeated navigation landmarks, and retain visible focus styles.

findings.summary: Text is not legible at a narrow mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: All representative 360px screenshots show the 768px tablet design scaled to roughly 47%, producing very small article metadata, navigation, and list copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow to one readable primary column at narrow widths, keep body text near 16 CSS px, and use comfortable line height/measure without viewport downscaling.

findings.summary: The experience fails narrow reflow and includes undersized targets.
findings.evidence: The 360px layout remained 769 CSS px wide and Lighthouse found 16px-high links below the 24px target-size floor.
findings.suggestedFix: Use `width=device-width, initial-scale=1`, remove fixed minimum widths, test at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom, and enlarge/space interactive targets.

findings.summary: Advertising requests produce repeated console/network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured repeated CORS failures to `hb.adingo.jp` plus unresolved/failed resources; the HAR also recorded ORB-blocked scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or correct broken ad integrations and gate optional requests so expected blocking does not flood the console or trigger failed work.

findings.summary: Image markup omits intrinsic dimensions and uses only legacy formats.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all 15 images missing at least one dimension and all 15 served as PNG/JPEG; eight below-fold images were not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height (or aspect-ratio), use AVIF/WebP responsive sources where beneficial, and lazy-load below-fold images.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and an unload handler reduce platform compatibility.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found three deprecations, including the main-frame unload listener, and confirmed that handler blocks BFCache restoration; source-map and Inspector Issues audits also failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide/visibility-safe patterns, remove deprecated ad APIs, restore useful source maps, and resolve DevTools issues.

findings.summary: Primary story links route through URLs explicitly blocked from crawling.
findings.evidence: Recon found many article links using `/redirector?...`; robots.txt disallows `/redirector` for all crawlers. Some header actions also expose empty href values.
findings.suggestedFix: Link directly to canonical article URLs in server HTML, reserve redirects for analytics fallback, and make every navigation action a crawlable href.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks a canonical URL.
findings.evidence: The home probe found no `rel=canonical`, although the page redirects to `?redirect=1`; the article template does provide a correct canonical and sitemaps are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a canonical to the clean homepage URL and keep redirect parameters out of canonical/indexing signals.

findings.summary: Article pages omit NewsArticle structured data.
findings.evidence: The article has accurate title, description, canonical, and Open Graph values, but the probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and no semantic `<time datetime>` values.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org `NewsArticle` JSON-LD with headline, dates, publisher, author, image, and canonical URL; use `<time datetime>` in visible metadata.

findings.summary: Security headers are absent and several cookies are not Secure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Cookie audit found five insecure cookies, including three 400-day analytics cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a report-only then enforced CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy; mark every HTTPS cookie Secure with the narrowest SameSite/domain/lifetime.

findings.summary: The page starts a broad tracking/advertising footprint before any visible choice.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 13 third-party origins and Google Analytics, GTM, Facebook, and Google ads; Lighthouse observed 18 third-party cookies. HAR attributes 52/55 requests and 1.61MB/1.63MB transferred bytes to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit each vendor, remove those without clear user value, defer optional analytics/ads until an appropriate consent or purpose signal, and minimise identifiers and retention.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP/Trusted Types foundation, or HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, strict referrer and permissions policies, HSTS, and a staged CSP; assess Trusted Types for DOM-XSS-sensitive code.

findings.summary: Publication dates are presented as unstructured locale-specific strings.
findings.evidence: Article metadata is rendered as `7/19(日) 11:04`; the article probe found no `<time datetime>` values, preventing unambiguous machine/locale interpretation.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit ISO timestamps in `<time datetime>`, format display values with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` for the selected locale, and preserve time-zone context.

findings.summary: Image delivery misses basic efficiency controls.
findings.evidence: All 15 audited images are JPEG/PNG, eight below-fold images are eager, and every image lacks at least one intrinsic dimension; Lighthouse estimated 156KiB image-delivery savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Negotiate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, lazy-load below-fold images, and provide intrinsic dimensions while retaining meaningful alt text.

findings.summary: Large optional scripts and failed ad requests perform wasteful work.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 1.30MB of scripts and failed ORB/analytics requests; Lighthouse reports 1,392KiB unused JS and 3.1s execution time.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove failed and unused integrations, conditionally import optional features, batch telemetry, and postpone background work until the main content is settled.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the page budget.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 1.61MB of 1.63MB transferred from third-party origins in this capture; Lighthouse’s broader run reached 3,491KiB and identified extensive tracking/cookie activity.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an enforceable third-party byte/request budget, load only vendors with measured value, and defer advertising/social SDKs until needed.

taskList.title: Build a real narrow responsive layout and restore focus/target usability
Cut render-blocking and unused JavaScript, especially third parties
Minimise tracking and harden cookies/response headers
Repair labels, heading landmarks, contrast, and visible focus
Make article links directly crawlable and add NewsArticle metadata
Remove broken integrations, deprecated APIs, and unload handlers
Add navigation continuity and reading-position cues
